messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text: 🚨 TickleBlurb: TickleWeb devs are releasing their (potentially) final functionality update to the collective group of nerds....This update provides a playoff simulation panel that a geek can dynamically update the standings by entering predicted results across remaining games.  The editable games should only show teams that can meaningfully impact the results of the selected team.  The functionality is only available for teams with <= 12 games remaining, so not very useful in the current season (currently).  Season 13 had a pretty good race where not everyone finished where you could check it out if you wanna get your rocks off. If you're looking at a team that's already clinched, you'll just see best/worst case scenarios for that particular team....Due to the potential sunset of TickleWeb, testing was half assed so just deal with it.

messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text: By the way, this can be accessed via the Standings slideout drawer (the same place the compare teams functionality is) - there's just an added tab at the top

messages.author: segathon
messages.text:
**The Taipei Dump**

Coined by the voice of the league, @Moses Bogart , the Taipei Dump is a C button dump icing performed as soon as you gain possession of the puck in your zone.

The move was primarily used by the youngest Bell brother, @NathanMB , aka “Jay’s Nate,” who, when he’s not traveling the world, is the owner of the Taipei Typhoons NHL ’95 team.

The move was meant to combat the aggressive “**Waterloo Forecheck**,” a style of play built around constant pressure on the puck.

When the 95 leagues of the world formed under one banner in the **WN95HL Online League**, created by the mad genius @UltraMagnus , it started as a gentleman’s game. When the puck changed hands, the other team went back on D.

Then the **Waterloo Tribe** finally joined the **"Dub"** in Season 2, and the gentleman’s game died.

Now it was chaos in the streets.

Every time the Right Defender cleaned up the puck, he was greeted by a relentless spam of C-button checks, with the intent of creating the dreaded  **"Dead Man" **and setting up a "**Sunnyvale Special Cross Crease**" goal.

messages.author: segathon
messages.text:
The rest of the league needed a counterbalance to this strategy. And there it was: the**" Taipei Dump"**, developed by the youngest Waterloo player, who had to do whatever he could just to survive against his older competition.

Get the puck. C-dump it immediately.

Do not do the A-dump, as **"Mark Lesser"** intended. That was too wild and uncontrollable, and it was much more likely to end up in the stands.

The C-dump could be controlled to some extent, much like one of @red bulls after he was ridden hard, sure it was still dangerous, but when the **"8 way directional" **dice was cast it could end up with the best result being a **"Dead Man" **on the other end. A truly tit-for-tat play.

The move has always been somewhat ridiculed by the league—not to the extent of the ** Down B** or **Goalie Obstruction** move, but it has been called “feminine” nonetheless.

But no one can argue that the move is still effective. And when the game is tight, with one mistake potentially leading to a goal, perhaps the only goal of the game, the **Taipei Dump** must be deployed.
